To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Ciliated glial cells are present in the interpeducular nucleus of the amphibian brain; 2. These glial cells are associated with neurons that contain one cilium;
ciliated glial cells are present in the interpedencular nucleus of the brain of the frog Rana escelenta and that the cilium is closely associated with a centriole and with a basal body.
ciliated glial cells in the frog brain have the same ultrastructural features of ciliated neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence of ciliated cells in the central nervous system of the frog.
the ultrastructure of the frog interpeduncular nuclei.
the study of the ultrastructure of the ciliated cells of the brain of the frog Rana escelenta.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the interpeducular nucleus of the Rana esculentum, cilia are present on neurons and glial elements.
the cilia of the interpedencular nucleus are not sensory, but are rather involved in the translocation of material from the cell body towards the perikaryon.
the cilium in the interpeducular nucleus of the Rana is not a sensory organ, but a specialized transport system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ciliated cells of the interpeuncular nucleus are glial cells which have a neuron-like appearance and which are probably involved in a transport mechanism.
ciliated glial cells in the frog interpeduncular nuclei have a role in neuronal transport.
the cilium complex of the interpeducular nucleus is a highly specialized organelle which has the morphological features of the centriole, basal body and cilium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cilium is not just a sensory organelle, but a dynamic organelle involved in the regulation of cell shape, cell division and cell polarity.
cilia are not just for swimming.
the cilium is not a simple appendage but is involved in the transport of materials from the cell body to the axon.
